additional_functions_note: redeemRate() (same-contract call) computes _redeemRate = (balanceOfBase * ONE) / totalSupply(); the relation's derivation of proxy (and hence _balances[to]) depends on this specific formula, though redeemRate's own internal statements are not drilled into per the atomic-dependency rule.
additional_contracts_note: IERC20(baseToken).balanceOf(address(this)) is an external call to the base-token contract; its returned baseBalance is a load-bearing input to proxy (and hence to the target value _balances[to]).
external_spec_note: No in-repo comment/NatSpec states the intended invariant that minted proxy-token balance must not exceed the base-token amount deposited (i.e., the redeem rate must not let baseBalance-derived proxy shares exceed 1:1 with amount); recognizing this as the correct bound requires understanding RebaseProxy's redeem-rate/peg design, which is protocol-specific, not derivable from source/language semantics alone.
case_notes: _mint(to, proxy) is OpenZeppelin ERC20's generic _mint, whose effect (_balances[to] += proxy; _totalSupply += proxy;) is a completely generic, protocol-independent ERC20 primitive. It is load-bearing (it is literally what defines the target value _balances[to]) but per Step 2 is recorded here as a case note rather than counted under Additional functions required, since its guarantee holds identically regardless of which contract calls it.
extraction_note: annotation_plans.md was not consulted (not needed for this case; the bug's shape is clear directly from the reconstructed source: mint() computes proxy from the contract's total post-deposit baseBalance rather than from the deposited amount alone, so proxy/shares can exceed the amount actually deposited if _redeemRate is manipulated below ONE). Debug-seeding block (@StateVar/@LocalVar/@IReturn under @Debugging) was read but is a separate RQ1-B concern, not part of this RQ2-A structural profile. Judgment call: to and amount are counted as ordinary parameter values (not excluded as mechanical plumbing like a loop index), since to is both the mapping key of the target value and an explicit _mint argument, and amount is the relation's own RHS operand. msg.sender/address(this)/baseToken (call-target identifiers) were excluded from the unique-values count as non-derivation-chain plumbing, consistent with the loop-index-exclusion rationale (they identify who/what to call, but don't feed the proxy/_balances[to] arithmetic).
